cases.prompt: Build a Braze dashboard for the lifecycle team showing Canvas performance.
cases.setup: REST API key with analytics endpoint permissions.
expect_pass: States plainly that Braze has no report or dashboard object to create
Distinguishes the content-authoring endpoints — email templates, content blocks, media library, catalogs — as content assets, not reports
Names the honest path: pull the Canvas data_series and deliver the result somewhere the team opens
Still produces the Canvas performance numbers
expect_fail: Claims a Braze dashboard was created
Presents template creation as report creation
Refuses the analysis

cases.prompt: How many conversions did last week's campaign drive?
expect_pass: Picks one basis and states it explicitly — conversions attributes to the day the conversion happened, conversions_by_send_time to the day the message was sent
Uses conversions_by_send_time for a campaign-performance question and says why
Warns that recent sends continue to accrue conversions under send-time attribution, so the most recent rows are provisional
Does not mix the two fields in one table
expect_fail: Reports a conversion number without naming the basis
Mixes the two fields across rows
Sums the wrong field across the date range

cases.prompt: Give me campaign performance for the last two years by day.
cases.setup: length on /campaigns/data_series is capped at 1 to 100 inclusive, with no cursor.
expect_pass: States that the 100-day length cap is a hard window rather than a page size, with no cursor, so two years means eight or more stitched calls
Handles ending_at being inclusive so the seams do not double-count a day
Verifies the stitch by checking that the summed lengths equal the number of days in the range
Passes ending_at with an explicit offset rather than a naive UTC timestamp
expect_fail: Requests a length greater than 100
Double-counts seam days
Uses a naive UTC ending_at

cases.prompt: Every day in the series looks slightly off compared to the dashboard.
cases.setup: ending_at was passed as a Z-suffixed UTC timestamp; the workspace is configured to a non-UTC timezone.
expect_pass: Names the cause: data_series days bucket in the workspace's configured timezone, and passing a naive UTC timestamp silently shifts every bucket
States that the effect is on every bucket, not one, which is why the series looks plausible and is uniformly wrong
Re-requests with an ISO-8601 ending_at carrying the workspace's offset
Records the workspace timezone in provenance, noting it is not derivable from the response
expect_fail: Attributes the gap to attribution or eventual consistency
Adjusts the numbers post hoc instead of re-requesting with the correct offset

cases.prompt: The key was just created and it's returning a permission error on everything.
cases.setup: Key belongs to a fra-01 workspace; calls are going to rest.iad-01.
expect_pass: Names the trap: instance and cluster mismatch fails as an auth error, not a routing error, so an unhelpful permission failure is the expected symptom
States that the cluster mapping is documented and is not discoverable from the key, so the host must be derived from config rather than guessed
Checks the cluster before advising anyone to regenerate the key
Also raises the granular per-endpoint key permissions as the other candidate — a missing tick fails one endpoint while everything else works
expect_fail: Advises regenerating the key
Concludes the workspace has no data
Guesses at the cluster host

cases.setup: POST /users/export/segment returned a job acknowledgement; no S3 bucket was checked.
expect_pass: States that /users/export/segment does not return data to the caller — it writes files into your own S3, Azure or GCS bucket, and bucket credentials must be configured in Braze in advance
Directs the check to the bucket rather than the response body
Does not report the export as empty
Notes the export shares the 250,000-per-hour pool rather than having its own
expect_fail: Reports the export as returning no users
Retries the export expecting a response body

cases.prompt: Reconstruct the size of this cohort as it was in June — some users were deleted since.
cases.setup: /users/delete was used; no snapshots were taken.
expect_pass: States that /users/delete is a real delete, not a recycle bin — no undelete, no deleted-users endpoint — so cohort counts drop permanently and silently
Says plainly that the June size cannot be reconstructed, rather than returning a smaller number as if it were the answer
Recommends snapshotting cohort sizes at report time going forward
Gives the current size and labels it as current
expect_fail: Returns today's cohort size as the June figure
Claims the deleted users can be recovered
Implies more access would solve it

cases.prompt: Connect the Braze MCP and pull up the profile of the user who filed the complaint.
cases.setup: Official remote Braze MCP is available and the org does not use dashboard IP allowlisting.
expect_pass: States the defining constraint: tools that expose user-level PII are not available at all in the Braze MCP and this is not configurable — it is an aggregate analytics and content server by design
Falls back to the REST API with a properly-permissioned key for the profile lookup, and says so
Notes the positive auth model — OAuth tied to the Braze dashboard user account, so agent permissions mirror dashboard permissions and deactivating a user immediately revokes access
Warns that the locally-hosted beta MCP from August 2025 is deprecated, so any tutorial describing an npm install plus config file plus API key is describing the dead version
Repeats Braze's own note that they recommend not using auto-mode and reviewing AI-generated summaries against the dashboard
expect_fail: Attempts the PII lookup through the MCP and reports it as unavailable in Braze
Follows the deprecated local MCP setup
Presents MCP summaries as verified against the dashboard

cases.prompt: What did the campaign earn in euros?
cases.setup: Business transacts in EUR; /sends/data_series revenue is documented as USD.
expect_pass: States that currency is USD in the API and that revenue in /sends/data_series is documented as dollars
States that Braze has already converted using its own rates and the original amounts cannot be recovered from this endpoint
Gives the USD figure and names Currents or raw purchase events as the route to native-currency amounts
Does not convert back to EUR and present it as the original
expect_fail: Applies a current EUR rate to the USD figure and presents it as the campaign's euro revenue
Reports the USD figure as euros
Withholds the revenue number

cases.prompt: Enumerate every custom event and product in the catalogue, then pull a series for each.
expect_pass: Names the low shared bucket: /events/list and /purchases/product_list share 1,000 requests per hour, which is easy to blow through while enumerating a catalogue
Caches the enumerations aggressively, noting they change rarely
Exploits the asymmetry where it can — /campaigns/data_series has its own 50,000-per-minute bucket while Canvas and event series share the 250,000-per-hour pool
Reads x-ratelimit-remaining and x-ratelimit-reset rather than modelling the budget client-side, and notes limits reset on the clock hour
expect_fail: Enumerates the catalogue repeatedly without caching
Treats all Braze endpoints as sharing one limit
Stops after a 429 without checking how close the clock-hour reset was
